rule: order = the order of the code slides of the deck; the page tab lists the examples by name in this order; each runs as setup + listing, with the library defined in the page

setup.code:
# setup: the chapter library of the page (L = chapter 11 library, R = the single regtest record of Bitcoin Core 31.1 inside the same wheel); the page boots these names
import sen0401_ch11_lib_v1_0_0 as L, hashlib
R = L.run()

examples.name: A block is a header, a count and transactions
examples.code:
g = L.chainparams_genesis('main')
size = 80 + 1 + g['tx_bytes']
core = R['b1_genesis']['block']['size']
(size, core, g['tx_bytes'])

examples.name: The 80-byte header has six fields
examples.code:
hx = R['b3_headers_480_489'][0]
b, h = bytes.fromhex(hx), L.header(hx)
cuts = [0, 4, 36, 68, 72, 76, 80]
widths = [y - x for x, y in zip(cuts, cuts[1:])]
(widths, len(b), h['bits'])

examples.name: Time, target and difficulty
examples.code:
t0 = L.chainparams_genesis('main')['time']
when = L.iso(t0)
mtp = L.median_time_past(R['b3_timestamps_110_121'])
tg = L.bits_to_target('1d00ffff')
diff = L.difficulty('1903a30c')
(when, mtp, tg.bit_length(), round(diff))

examples.name: The headline in the genesis block
examples.code:
g = L.chainparams_genesis('main')
msg = g['message']
zeros = L.leading_zero_hex(g['hash'])
(msg[:24], zeros)

show.expected: 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks'

examples.name: A block's name is the hash of its header
examples.code:
g = L.chainparams_genesis('main')
b = bytes.fromhex(g['header'])
once = hashlib.sha256(b).digest()[::-1].hex()
twice = L.sha256d(b)[::-1].hex()
(once[:12], twice == g['hash'])

examples.name: Height in the coinbase and coinbase maturity
examples.code:
c = R['b3_bip34']
heights = sorted(L.bip34_height(v) for v in c.values())
m = R['b7_maturity']
a, b = m['confirmations_99'], m['confirmations_100']
ok = [a['allowed'], b['allowed']]
(heights, ok)

examples.name: Back-links make the history hard to change
examples.code:
hs = R['b3_headers_480_489']
p = [L.header(x) for x in hs]
link = lambda x, y: y['prev'] == x['hash']
ok = sum(map(link, p, p[1:]))
t = L.tamper_chain(hs, 3)
(ok, t['broken_links'], t['must_remine'])

examples.name: Forks and the attacker's odds
examples.code:
f = R['b6_fork']
same = f['prev1'] == f['prev2'] == f['parent']
grew = f['active_is'] == f['extension']
cu = lambda z: round(L.catchup(0.1, z), 7)
odds = [cu(z) for z in (0, 1, 2, 6)]
(same, grew, odds)

examples.name: The merkle tree: many transactions, one root
examples.code:
b = R['b4_blocks']['4']
lv = [len(x) for x in L.merkle_levels(b['txids'])]
root = L.merkle_root(b['txids']) == b['merkleroot']
o = R['b4_blocks']['3']
lo = [len(x) for x in L.merkle_levels(o['txids'])]
(lv, lo, root)

examples.name: A merkle proof is a short path of hashes
examples.code:
b = R['b4_blocks']['16']
ids = b['txids']
p = L.merkle_path(ids, 10)
good = L.follow_path(ids[10], p) == b['merkleroot']
size = (len(p), 32 * len(p))
sizes = [32 * L.depth(n) for n in (1024, 4096, 16000)]
(size, good, sizes)

examples.name: Two weaknesses of the merkle tree
examples.code:
ids = [L.sha256d(bytes([i])).hex() for i in range(1, 7)]
twin = ids + [ids[4], ids[5]]
same = L.merkle_root(ids) == L.merkle_root(twin)
m = R['b5_mutation']
(same, m['n_original'], m['n_mutated'])

examples.name: A light client verifies with a few hashes
examples.code:
pm = R['b4_proof_for_k_of_16']['proof_hex']
mb = L.parse_merkleblock(pm)
n, k = mb['ntx'], len(mb['hashes'])
(n, k, mb['total'])

ports

examples.name: Signet: the challenge script and the magic
examples.code:

ops = L.script_ops(c)
magic = L.signet_magic(c)

examples.name: Regtest: halving every 150 blocks
examples.code:
half = L.chain_facts('regtest')['halving']
hs = ['1', '149', '150', '299', '300', '450']
btc = [L.subsidy(int(h), half) / 10**8 for h in hs]
s = R['b2_subsidy']
same = all(L.subsidy(int(h), half) == s[h] for h in s)
(half, btc, same)
